newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Banks should take care on HK mortgages - HKMA.
newsitem.headline: Banks should take care on HK mortgages - HKMA.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority said banks should exercise additional care in relation to their property exposure following recent sharp increases in property prices, particularly at the upper end of the market.
The HKMA said outstanding mortgages by 33 institutions surveyed rose 1.8 percent in November on the month, above the average 1.5 percent increase of the previous 12 months.
The Acting Deputy Chief Executive of HKMA, Raymond Li, noted the increase in November followed a sharp rise in October, reversing the slowing growth trend of some previous months.
"At the same time, property prices, particularly those at the upper end of the market, have risen sharply in recent weeks and there are signs of renewed speculative activity," he said.

"In this environment, institutions need to exercise additional care in relation to their property exposure. They should look critically at their lending criteria, particularly in relation to the more expensive properties where the speculation has been most evident," he said.

Li said that as an overall policy, institutions should adhere strictly to the 70 percent loan-to-value ratio in respect of their own lending exposure and should avoid arrangements which circumvent this.
"A lower ratio than 70 percent will normally be appropriate for more expensive properties, and the valuation of such properties should be carefully examined," he said.

Li said institutions should also pay attention to whether the property will be owner-occupied is being acquired for investment purposes, and added the HKMA will continue to monitor the situation closely. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843-6441
